title: Corporate Group Travel Checklist: Planning Flights for Conferences and Offsites
metaDescription: A practical checklist for booking corporate group flights for conferences, sales meetings and team offsites, from budgeting to name deadlines.
content:
Flying a team to a conference, sales kick-off or offsite involves more than booking seats. Use this checklist to keep your corporate group trip on budget and on schedule.

1. Set the budget and travel policy

  • Agree who flies economy, premium economy or business class.
  • Decide who approves bookings and changes.
  • Confirm how costs are billed: one company invoice or individual cards.

2. Map where everyone is flying from

Teams often depart from several offices. List every origin city and the number of travelers from each, so the agent can build separate group blocks that arrive around the same time.

3. Fix the event dates and arrival window

Give your travel agent the first session time and the last event, so flights can land with enough buffer and depart after the closing session.

4. Request group quotes 3 to 6 months ahead

Early requests secure better fares and give you time for internal approvals before deposits are due.

5. Track the key deadlines

  • Deposit due date
  • Final name submission
  • Final payment and ticketing
  • Last date to release unused seats

6. Collect traveler details

You will need each traveler's full name as shown on their ID or passport, date of birth, and any frequent flyer numbers, meal requests or accessibility needs.

7. Plan for changes

Attendee lists always change. Ask how many name changes are included and what happens if someone cancels after ticketing.
